name: SpaceX
day_summary: BOND SHOCK — TWO-CONSECUTIVE-CLOSE FRAMEWORK BLOWN OUT. SPCX closed at $165.78 on June 22, down from the official prior close of $174.90 (-5.21%, -$9.12). This masks a brutal intraday reversal: SPCX opened near $185 on IG ratings pricing-in (the gap-up materialized as expected), then CRASHED approximately -16% from the session peak after SpaceX announced a $20 billion inaugural bond offering (senior unsecured notes, proceeds to repay the xAI bridge loan). The intraday pattern: gap to $185 (Day 1 watch activated) → bond offering announcement → collapse to intraday low near $160 → partial recovery to close $165.78. The result: SPCX closed BELOW the $185 two-consecutive-close re-entry gate, BELOW the $174.90 official prior close, and the Day 1 confirmation that the morning dossier was tracking DID NOT materialize as a daily CLOSE. The two-consecutive-close framework is FULLY RESET — it needs TWO NEW CONSECUTIVE CLOSES above $185 from scratch. Capital structure context: $75B IPO (June 12) + $60B Cursor AI acquisition (stock deal) + $20B bond offering = $155B in capital movements in 10 days. The IG ratings floor remains intact (Moody's Baa1, S&P BBB, Fitch BBB+) but the equity market is repricing the capital structure. Step Aside at HIGH conviction maintained.

The intraday gap to $185 materialized as expected, but the $20B bond offering announcement destroyed the daily close confirmation. This is EXACTLY why the two-consecutive-close daily close rule exists — intraday peaks are not re-entry signals. Framework is now fully reset: SPCX must close above $185 on two consecutive days on above-average volume. Capital structure re-pricing is not complete; $155B in 10 days of capital movements requires multiple sessions to fully digest. Re-entry framework restart: Day 1 candidate is now June 23 (if SPCX closes above $185) — this would require a ~+11.6% recovery from $165.78; unlikely without a major catalyst. Most probable re-entry window: post-September 2 first earnings report (once disclosed financials are available). IG ratings floor at $165+ (Moody's Baa1 prevents collapse to $135 IPO price). Maintain step aside — do not touch.

84x revenue multiple unchanged at $185 — IG ratings lower the cost of capital but they don't lower the revenue multiple; at $185 and $2.54T market cap, SPCX still requires Starlink growing >40% annually to September 2 earnings plus Starship recurring revenue plus Cursor AI contribution to justify the valuation; none of those fundamentals were disclosed in the rating agencies' assessments.

December 9 lock-up expiry is 170 days away — any investor who buys at $185 must be comfortable holding through the first major float expansion; lock-up expiry typically creates selling pressure 30–60 days before the event; the 84x multiple with approaching lock-up creates a ceiling on the re-rating until September 2 earnings reveals the disclosed financial picture.

MSCI passive bid exhausting (Day 11+) — the MSCI systematic rebalancing buying window that supported Days 1–10 post-IPO is largely exhausted; the volume needed to sustain >$185 (ideally >100M shares daily close volume) must come from genuine institutional conviction, not passive mechanics; IG ratings help, but the July expiry OI structure is the arbiter.
